title: main is RED: `Build Docs` fails on `SchemaNode` vs `SchemaRenderer`'s `schema` prop — the docs site has not built since #4608 landed
body:
**Corrected after filing** — the original framing ("CI never runs apps/site's type-check") was wrong, and the truth is worse: CI runs it inside `next build`, and it has been failing on `main` since PR #4608 merged. The corrected version follows; the false half is retracted at the bottom so the record is not silently rewritten.

Measured while implementing (d1) of #4600 (PR #4615). Filed unassigned. Duplicate-searched: no open issue covers it.

## main is red

`ci.yml`'s **Build Docs** job runs `pnpm --filter @object-ui/site build`, i.e. `next build`, and Next runs TypeScript as part of that build. The `main` push run for `c1d939f7f` — the merge of PR #4608, *"fix(types): one SchemaNode and one label vocabulary — the union wins"* (#4580) — failed:

```
run 31740683664   main   push   c1d939f7f   conclusion: failure
  Build Docs -> step "Build Site" -> failure
  (the immediately preceding main run, 31736774667, was success)
```

and the failing step's log is exactly:

```
app/components/InteractiveDemo.tsx(74,43):  error TS2322: Type 'SchemaNode' is not assignable to type 'string | BaseSchema | null | undefined'.
app/components/InteractiveDemo.tsx(119,35): error TS2322: (same)
app/components/LiveSplitDemo.tsx(286,37):   error TS2322: (same)
app/components/SchemaThumbnail.tsx(145,35): error TS2322: (same)
app/playground/page.tsx(1413,39):           error TS2322: (same)
  Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'string | BaseSchema | null | undefined'.
Failed to type check.
```

Every PR branched after that commit inherits the red — PR #4615 does, and its own gates (Lint, Type Check, Control Byte Scan, Changeset, Docs Link Check, Build and E2E) are all green beside it.

## The contract skew underneath

This is not an app bug. `@object-ui/core` exports `SchemaNode`; `@object-ui/react` exports `SchemaRenderer`; and after #4580 made the union canonical, passing the former to the latter's `schema` prop no longer type-checks. `SchemaNode` now includes primitives — `number` is the member the error names — while the prop takes `string | BaseSchema | null | undefined`. Any consumer that types a value as `SchemaNode` and renders it hits this; `apps/site` is simply the consumer that lives in this repo and is compiled by CI.

So the decision is a contract one and belongs with #4580's ruling, not with a cast at five call sites:

1. **Widen `SchemaRenderer`'s `schema` prop to `SchemaNode`** — consistent with "the union wins", and the renderer already has to cope with whatever it is handed at runtime. A published prop-type change in `@object-ui/react`, so it needs a changeset and a look at what else reads that prop type.
2. **Keep the prop narrow and say the union is not what a host holds** — then the five call sites are wrong and each needs a real narrowing (not `as never`), and the guidance that came with #4580 needs to say so.

⛔ Casting at the call sites to get CI green would be the consumer-side tolerance that AGENTS.md's contract-first rule exists to prevent — it hides the skew in the exact place the next author will copy it from.

## Second, smaller half (still true)

`apps/site`'s type-check script is named `types:check`, not `type-check`, so `turbo run type-check` (the `Type Check` job) skips it and `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` reports it as its "1 not compiled" package. That is why the `Type Check` job is green while `Build Docs` is red on the same commit — the type errors are only reached through `next build`, three minutes later in a different job. Renaming the script would surface this class in the job named after it, and is worth doing alongside whichever option above is chosen.

## Retraction

The first version of this issue claimed "CI never runs it". False — `Build Docs` does, via `next build`. The claim came from noticing the turbo task-name gap and not checking whether another job compiled the package anyway. The gap is real; the conclusion drawn from it was not.

Refs #4600, PR #4615, #4580, PR #4608.
